transcript: Last night, my friend AJ and I went to Rob Ryan’s solo show Mascot. It’s a hybrid, kind of autobiographical, stand- up-storytelling situation, where Rob jokes his way through some experiences he had growing up in a dysfunctional family. He discusses his mother's alcoholism, his brother's depression and family tragedies so extreme, that you’d think most families wouldn't be able to recover from them. But Rob's way of telling these tales, and perhaps of coping with them, is through humor. Of the solo stand up storytelling type shows that I've seen, this one felt the most like a stand up routine. Rob responds to how his stories are landing and resonating in the room rather than adhering to a particularly theatrical structure. And honestly he doesn't really need to do anything more because the story is already very compelling as it is. I very much enjoyed this piece and I had some laughs but I must say, I really found it to be profoundly sad. But I enjoy sad stories, so if that's your jam too, Mascot is running at Soho Playhouse through December 16th.
